title: Data, analysis and visualization
text: Within a stated detour allowance, can a pedestrian reduce estimated direct-sun exposure compared with a shortest walking route? The present experiment examines building-shadow scenarios in Center City Philadelphia. Citywide walking routes provide broader geographic context without extrapolating shade to areas with missing data.

title: Data, analysis and visualization
text: Within a stated detour allowance, can a pedestrian reduce estimated direct-sun exposure compared with a shortest walking route? The present experiment examines building-shadow scenarios in Center City Philadelphia. Citywide walking routes provide broader geographic context without extrapolating shade to areas with missing data.

title: Data, analysis and visualization
text:
Collection

OpenStreetMap: a bounding-box Overpass API query retrieves Philadelphia street geometry and access tags. The prior building extract contains 2,649 closed-way footprints. Data retrieved November 10, 2026. OSM attribution and ODbL.
US Census: the TIGERweb ACS 2024 service supplies Philadelphia’s municipal boundary.
City of Philadelphia: the place-name directory is paginated through its ArcGIS API. The AIS service geocodes user-submitted addresses. Address queries are sent to that service only when a user submits or selects a result.

The light-gray basemap uses Esri tiles and labels for context; it is not analytical input. No paid API key is configured.

title: Data, analysis and visualization
text:
Analysis in Python
python/fetch_data.py acquires the city boundary and street inputs. python/prepare_data.py filters roads by mapped access and highway type, constructs a directed OSMnx graph and simplifies its geometry. Explicit pedestrian one-way tags are respected. Motor vehicle one-way rules are not automatically applied to pedestrians. Graph geometry extends up to 500 m beyond the boundary to preserve nearby connections; endpoint searches are restricted to the city.
GeoPandas, Shapely and pyproj transform geometry to EPSG:26918 for length and shadow calculations. Building height comes from OSM height, then floor count ×3 m, then a 12 m default. 974 of 2,649 heights use the default. Relation/multipolygon buildings from OSM are absent from this extract.
For hourly July 15, 2026 scenarios (8 AM–7 PM EDT), a NOAA fractional-year solar-position approximation supplies elevation and azimuth. Footprints and projected wall faces form ground-shadow polygons. Road samples spaced approximately 10 m apart are tested against their union. This is a physical geometric model, not trained machine learning.
python/routing.py uses A* on the directed network. The shortest route is the baseline. Seven exposure penalties generate alternatives; the least-exposed candidate within the extra-time allowance is retained. This search does not guarantee the globally optimal solution to the constrained problem. Unknown-shade edges are excluded from shade-optimized searches.
Locations snap to the nearest graph node, with a 150 m (approximately 490 ft) maximum. Snap gaps and crossing waits are excluded from the reported trip time and distance and are disclosed in the dashboard. A nearby disconnected path can cause a route failure; this is not evidence that a real-world trip is impossible.

title: Data, analysis and visualization
text:
Visualization and deployment
python/app.py uses Panel, a DeckGL map pane and Bokeh charts. The Python routing and search callbacks run in a Pyodide worker on GitHub Pages. Browser libraries generated by the framework render the map; handwritten JavaScript is not part of the new app’s routing or interaction logic. This Quarto site documents collection, analysis and visualization separately from the map.
Map routes, exposure bars and same-route time profiles respond to route, time and detour controls. The hourly chart re-evaluates the selected two paths at each hour; it does not optimize a new path at each plotted point.

title: Data, analysis and visualization
text:
Checks and limitations
python/check.py compares four real trips with an independent NetworkX Dijkstra calculation, checks detour and exposure bounds, rejects same-node/outside-city endpoints, serializes a Panel document, and exercises successful/failed search callbacks. python/data/checks.json records the outcome. The AIS endpoint returned a valid point for 1234 Market St and a permissive cross-origin response header during API verification. Browser rendering and interactive click-through checks remain pending.
This is not live temperature, verified sidewalk navigation, a cooling-center availability service, or an AI model. Trees, terrain, bridges/tunnels, sidewalk side, changing shade during a trip and actual weather are not modeled. Boundary effects and assumed heights can materially change exposure estimates. Field testing is still needed.

title: Data, analysis and visualization
text:
Course connection
The work provides substantive implementations of API collection, geospatial operations, OSMnx network analysis, a Panel deployment, multiple linked interactive views, and integration of OSM, Census and city-government data. These are candidate requirement mappings for instructor review, not a claim that the final project is finished. Raster analysis, clustering and machine learning have not been added merely to increase a requirement count.
The full report, final presentation and written proposal approval remain separate course deliverables.

title: A little more shade. A better way there.
text:
Open the interactive map →
Search a Philadelphia street address or place name, choose a matching result, and compare your walk. Try 1234 Market St, Rittenhouse Square, or LOVE Park. Adjust the time of day and the extra minutes you are willing to walk. Distances are shown in miles and feet.
The first visit downloads a Python runtime and about 12 MB of prepared geographic data. Please allow time for the loading screen to finish. This preview needs an internet connection and a browser with WebGL.

title: A little more shade. A better way there.
text:
What changed

Typed addresses and places: Philadelphia’s address API and a directory of 5,996 official place-name records replace the fixed list of endpoints. Some names have several matches.
Citywide walking network: 138,753 nodes and 421,248 directed connections prepared with OSMnx. Some disconnected paths and imperfect entrance locations remain.
Python implementation: GIS preprocessing, route calculation, address search and dashboard callbacks are authored in Python. Panel generates the browser rendering code.
Linked map and charts: route choice, summer hour and detour allowance update the comparison. Download the resulting route metrics as CSV.

title: A little more shade. A better way there.
text:
What the results mean
Building-shadow coverage is still limited to the amber Center City rectangle. Outside it, the app shows a regular walking route and its coverage percentage. Missing shade data is gray in the chart and is excluded from full-route shade comparisons.

title: A little more shade. A better way there.
text:
Preview status
This is a Python migration preview, not the completed course submission. Native routing and dashboard checks are documented in the repository. Browser visual and click-through verification remains pending because the preview tool reached its usage limit. GPS location is not implemented; typed origins are supported.
